Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

IsoriX (development version)

Bug fixes

  • isofit() (and thus isomultifit()) did not fix the residual variance of the residual dispersion model to its theoretical expectation (phi = 2) when spaMM_method = list(disp_model = "HLfit"), so this variance was estimated instead, contrary to what happens with the other fitting methods and to what the documentation states. Fits obtained with "HLfit" and "fitme" are now identical.
  • printing (or summarising) isoscapes, fitted isoscapes, calibration fits and assignments no longer displays stray NULL lines (#220).
  • prepraster() failed to crop the raster according to the sources when given the output of isomultifit(), since this type of object was not recognised.
  • isomultiscape() did not check that the names of the layers of the raster used for weighting match those of the fits, since the check looked for an element that does not exist.
  • prepraster() now respects verbose = FALSE (it used to always print the raster).
  • the plotting functions for isoscapes and assignments no longer crash when the user provides their own country borders (borders = list(borders = ...)) containing more than one polygon.
  • the test of spatial extrapolation performed by calibfit() no longer produces false positives: calibration sites located on the boundary of the convex hull formed by the source sites (e.g. sharing the location of a source site) are now considered to be inside, longitudes are handled consistently whether expressed within [-180, 180) or [0, 360) and hulls straddling the antimeridian (180 degrees) are now handled correctly (#200).
  • ?plot now opens the documentation of the IsoriX plotting functions instead of the generic page listing re-exported functions (#193).
  • passing an empty list to a list argument (e.g. isofit(data, mean_model_fix = list())) no longer triggers an error; it now means that all defaults are kept (#206).
  • when plotting individual assignments, each map now only shows the location of the sample it corresponds to, instead of the locations of all samples (#103).

New features

  • isomultifit() and isomultiscape() can now fit the models and build the isoscapes of the different strata (e.g. months) in parallel, using the new argument Ncpu (by default set by the global option Ncpu, i.e. 2L unless changed with options_IsoriX(); use Ncpu = 1 for sequential computations). Parallel computing relies on socket clusters from the base package parallel and thus works on Windows, macOS and Linux. The outputs are identical whether computed sequentially or in parallel, and what is printed, as well as messages and warnings, are still displayed. For the 12 monthly fits of GNIPDataDE, the fitting time dropped from about 33 s to 19 s using 4 CPUs (#52).
  • new method AIC() for the outputs of isofit() and isomultifit(), which computes the conditional AIC of the fitted isoscapes corrected for the number of parameters estimated in the residual dispersion model (following Courtiol & Rousset 2017). This allows for the comparison of models differing in their residual dispersion model, and not only in their mean model. When several fits are given (e.g. AIC(fit1, fit2)), a table is returned which also details the number of parameters of each model and the uncorrected conditional AIC (#101).
  • new function plot_sources() mapping, for aggregated source data (as produced by prepsources()), the mean, standard deviation and number of measurements at each source location, using either coloured points or text labels; in interactive sessions, the user is asked to press before each new map (#195).
  • new function calibscape() to build calibrated isoscapes, i.e. to convert an isoscape of source isotopic values (e.g. precipitation) into an isoscape of sample isotopic values (e.g. animal tissues) using a calibration fit. Only the mean isoscape is calibrated. The output, of class CALIBSCAPE (in addition to ISOSCAPE), can be plotted (which = "mean" only; by default, the plot shows the location of the calibration samples instead of that of the sources, see the new argument calibs of plot.ISOSCAPE()) but cannot be used by isofind() or create_aliens() (#191).
  • new function plot_dependencies() plotting the packages that IsoriX requires and suggests, and the dependencies among them, which can help with installation problems (#171).
  • prepsources() no longer requires the columns year and month unless data are filtered or split by year or month, and the column elev is now optional (#192, #123).
  • IsoriX now handles areas crossing the International Date Line (antimeridian) out of the box, e.g. for studies centred on the Pacific (#180):
    • prepsources() can select sources across the International Date Line using long_min > long_max (e.g. long_min = 70, long_max = -150);
    • getelev() can download elevation across the International Date Line using long_min > long_max: since elevatr only handles longitudes within [-180, 180], the area is downloaded in two parts which are assembled into a single raster with continuous longitudes (e.g. from 70 to 210);
    • isofit() and isomultifit() express longitudes within [0, 360] instead of [-180, 180] when the sources straddle the International Date Line, so that the area they cover is continuous (a message is displayed);
    • prepraster() crops structural rasters across the International Date Line, both manually (manual_crop with a first longitude greater than the second one, which no longer triggers a warning) and automatically from a fitted model;
    • isoscape(), calibfit(), isofind() and prepcipitate() handle such rasters and express locations consistently (e.g. the ocean mask of isofind() now also applies beyond 180 degrees);
    • the plotting functions automatically shift country borders, masks and the locations of sources, calibration and assignment samples, so that they are drawn properly on maps crossing the International Date Line.

Minor changes

  • the R package is now stored at the root of the GitHub repository instead of in a sub-folder: the development version is thus installed with remotes::install_github("courtiol/IsoriX") (instead of "courtiol/IsoriX/IsoriX"), and tools requiring the package at the root of the repository, such as rhub::rhub_setup(), now work (#185).
  • isoscape() (and thus isomultiscape()) is faster for large rasters: predictions are now computed in a single call to spaMM per model, letting spaMM slice the computation of the prediction variances into larger blocks, instead of calling spaMM on chunks of 1000 locations. The isoscapes produced are unchanged; for a raster of 600,000 cells, the computation time is divided by about 4. The progress bar is now the one from spaMM (shown when verbose = TRUE). The size of these blocks can be set with the new global option spaMM_blocksize (default 16000L; e.g. options_IsoriX(spaMM_blocksize = 4000L) to reduce the memory used on very large rasters). The unused internal function .futureisoscape() has been removed (#150, #176).
  • IsoriX now requires spaMM >= 4.4.0 (for the function DoF()).
  • the main functions now check the type of the objects given to them and stop with an informative error message saying which function creates the expected object (e.g. when an isoscape is given instead of the output of isofit()), or that source data must first be aggregated with prepsources() (#164).
  • each reference cited in the documentation now includes a link to its DOI, and citation("IsoriX") now gives the pages and the DOI of the book chapter describing IsoriX.
  • the titles of the help pages of all datasets follow a consistent pattern indicating their role in the workflow (e.g. “Calibration data: …”), and those of datasets from different studies are no longer identical (#97).
  • outdated links in the documentation were updated (e.g. the homepage of spaMM in ?isofit and the link to the preprint in citation("IsoriX")), following the review of all links with the new script release_checks/list_links.R (#188).
  • the dataset CountryBorders contains again the names of the countries (column name), so that countries can be selected by name, e.g. CountryBorders[CountryBorders$name == "Germany", ] (#183). CountryBorders and OceanMask have been recreated from the current version of the Natural Earth data (same resolution as before), which leads to minor changes in borders (e.g. Tuvalu is now included).
  • the titles of isoscape plots no longer refer to hydrogen by default, since IsoriX cannot know which isotope is being studied: the default of the global option title_delta_notation is now NULL. Use e.g. options_IsoriX(title_delta_notation = bquote(delta^2*H)) to restore the previous titles. The documentation (?options_IsoriX and the bookdown) now also explains what to do when the delta symbol is not rendered by the graphic device (#155).
  • prepsources() now stops with an informative message when the data have already been aggregated or when required columns are missing (#139).
  • isofit() now stops with an informative message if elevation is used as a predictor but is absent from the data.
  • prepraster() and isoscape() now stop with an informative message when the structural raster is no longer valid in the current R session (e.g. a raster read from a file and restored from a saved workspace), instead of the obscure error “NULL value passed as symbol address” produced by terra.
  • the link to the IAEA WISER portal no longer points to an .aspx page (#186).
  • isofit() now displays a message, once per R session, when the default model (without any fixed-effect predictor) is fitted, to encourage users to compare alternative models; a new section of the online documentation explains how to do so (#204).

Internal (geeky) changes

  • the tests now use the third edition of testthat and run in parallel (using 2 processes by default, or the number given by the environment variable TESTTHAT_CPUS), which makes them about twice as fast. During checks, each test process uses a single thread for linear algebra, since multithreaded libraries such as OpenBLAS otherwise make the processes compete for the cores (the README of the GitHub repository shows how to run devtools::test() this way).
  • tibble is now a suggested package, so that the support of tibbles is tested using genuine tibbles.
  • the documentation is now generated using roxygen2 8.1.1.
  • GitHub issue templates have been added (#178).

IsoriX 0.9.4

CRAN release: 2026-01-13

Main release goal

  • the documentation had to be migrated to another website, so all links were updated.

Minor changes

  • bookdown.org is being discontinued so the bookdown has been migrated to “https://courtiol-isorix.share.connect.posit.cloud”.

Internal (geeky) changes

  • now explicitly depends on R (>= 4.1.0) since we use pipes (|>).

IsoriX 0.9.3

CRAN release: 2024-09-08

New features

  • a new global option title_delta_notation is available to modify the delta notation for all plotted isoscapes. The can be use, for example, to fix some issues with the display of the delta character, or for using another stable isotope than deuterium. See ?options_IsoriX for details.
  • new datasets CalibDataBatRev, CalibDataBat2Rev, AssignDataRev and AssignData2Rev which are revised version of CalibDataBat,CalibDataBat2,AssignDataandAssignData2` (respectively). The bat fur isotope values were corrected to align with the current delta values for keratin reference materials (Soto et al. 2017, https://doi.org/10.1002/rcm.7893) ensuring comparability between formerly and more recently normalized datasets of delta values for deuterium.

Breaking changes

  • the dataset CalibDataBat2 now contains slightly different elevation values (the one reported by field workers as opposed to those extracted from a specific elevation map).
  • the dataset CalibDataBat now contains different values for the column “site_ID”.

Major changes

  • the functions prepsources(), calibfit() and isofind() emit warnings if some locations share the same location IDs or if several locations IDs correspond to a unique location. This should help users to spot issues in their data (fixes #133).

Minor changes

  • the functions terra::extract() and lattice::lpolygon() now re-exported and lattice::panel.points()) no longer is.

Small fixes

  • the URL for WorldClim data was outdated so getprecip() was no longer working.
  • some internal code had arguments misspelt. It was working as a result of R’s ability to do partial matching, but this was not good practice. It is now fixed (fixes #181).
  • some links in the documentation were incomplete and flagged is some online CRAN checks (“Found the following Rd file(s) with Rd targets missing package”). This should now be fixed.
  • function names should now be consistently displayed as computer code in the documentation.

Internal (geeky) changes

  • the project is now being setup so that the development using VScode is possible.
  • the format of the NEWS file has been changed to allow for using usethis::use_github_release() to create new releases (fixes #177).
  • the description of datasets now relies on the markdown syntax.

IsoriX 0.9.2

CRAN release: 2023-11-14

Main release goal

  • This release restores some key features that had been lost after dropping the direct dependencies raster and sp in v0.9.1.:
    • the possibility to save and reload objects created by IsoriX (now via saveRDS() and readRDS()). (#172)
    • the possibility to plot oceans and other masks containing “holes” (thanks to changes in lattice and rasterVis). (#169, #170)

Breaking changes

As compared to IsoriX versions < 0.9.1, the following changes may break existing code:

  • code for plots:

    layer(sp.polygons(CountryBorders, col = "white")) +
layer(sp.polygons(OceanMask, col = "white", fill = "lightgreen"))

    now needs to be replaced by:

    layer(lpolygon(CountryBorders, border = "white")) +
layer(lpolygon(OceanMask, border = "white", col = "lightgrey"))

    Notice both the change in the function used to plot polygons and the change in the arguments used to control the colour of the borders and the colour of the fill. Similarly, the function sp.points() should be replaced by lpoints() and so on.

  • saving and reloading objects save() & load() can no longer be used, one must instead use saveRDS() & readRDS().

New features

  • the NEWS (contained in this file) are now stored in NEWS.md rather than in inst/NEWS.Rd and use a markdown syntax.
  • it is now possible to have missing values in predictors used to build isoscapes and in the isoscapes themselves.

Major changes

  • plotting methods for polygons, lines and points have been removed from IsoriX and are now handled by lattice and rasterVis.

  • new S3 and S4 methods saveRDS() for objects of the class ISOSCAPE, CALIBFIT & ISOFIND (see ?serialize for details).

  • new S3 and S4 method readRDS() which should be able to read objects created in IsoriX, as well as objects created with terra and objects created otherwise.

    In case of issues reading RDS files not created by IsoriX, try using base::readRDS() with the namespace base:: mentioned explicitly and please let us know of this issue.

Minor changes

  • the bookdown is now listed in DESCRIPTION.
  • some old URLs have been updated.

Bug fixes

  • the function isomultiscape() was still using raster instead of terra.
  • the object PrecipBrickDE was still using raster instead of terra.

Internal (geeky) changes

  • new function .safe_and_quiet_predictions() which turns wraps around spaMM::predict.HLfit(), turns warnings into messages, allows not to display the same messages many times, and outputs NAs when spaMM::predict.HLfit() fails. For testing, options_IsoriX(spaMM_debug = TRUE) may be used to restore the original behaviour of spaMM::predict.HLfit().
  • the classes ISOSCAPE, CALIBFIT & ISOFIND are now also defined as S4 classes, which was necessary to design methods for saveRDS() which are compatible with terra.
  • the package now contains a WORDLIST file which is used by devtools::spell_check() (via spelling::spell_check_package) to check for typos in the documentation.
  • fixed various | or & which should have always been || or && (spotted via lintr::lint_package()).
  • fixed various sequences of the form 1:... which should have always been handled by seq_along or seq_len to avoid NULL issues (spotted via lintr::lint_package()).
  • package withr now suggested; we use it to automatically delete a file created during testing (using withr::defer).
  • instead of one Rproj file used to handle both the package and the bookdown development, we now rely on 2 Rproj files, which solves some limitations encountered with usethis.
